title: Viva Engage: handle GDPR deletion requests in the Engage admin center
summary: The deletion API call needs correction: without the GDPR query parameter, the published call suspends the user instead of submitting an erasure request. The roadmap details and documented removal workflow are supported, but the assurances about no user-facing change and all removal options being irreversible go beyond the evidence.

claims.quote: Network admins, Verified admins & Engage admins can use the Manage GDPR data subject requests module in the Viva Engage admin center to process data subject requests for GDPR.

claims.where: Governance controls: opening sentence; rationale: risk
claims.claim: All of the module's removal options are irreversible.
claims.quote: Searched: "Permanently remove this user, but retain their messages" "undo". Read module, GDPR guidance and REST deletion reference; the module labels the second option irreversible and erasure irreversible after 14 days, but does not state that for every option.
claims.fix: Replace 'The removal options are irreversible' with 'Removing a user and their messages cannot be reversed, and Erase this user cannot be undone after 14 days'. In the risk rationale replace 'those options cannot be reversed' with the same specific qualification. Do not assert that the first option is reversible or irreversible.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Two of the three module options are documented as irreversible, one immediately and one after 14 days.
claims.quote: Permanently remove this user, and remove their messages ... You can't reverse this action. ... Erase this user. Wipe their name and personal information, but leave their messages (Can't be undone after 14 days)

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: The REST endpoint offers programmatic GDPR erasure as an alternative to using the admin-center erase option.
claims.quote: gdpr_delete=true — submits a GDPR deletion request. Asynchronously erases the user’s PII across systems and anonymizes authored content (messages remain but are no longer attributable).

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: Microsoft cautions against API-based user deletion for routine lifecycle management because it can cause unrecoverable data loss.
claims.quote: User lifecycle management should generally be performed through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center or Microsoft Entra. API-based user deletions may lead to unrecoverable data loss and are therefore not recommended.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: After the 14-day erase window, remaining files and messages are marked as belonging to a former user.
claims.quote: After the 14-day window, files and messages remain, but are marked as belonging to a former user.
